content.comment_body: Modifying the file "render.js" removes the unwanted "16 #" when showing analog values using HEX format in the extended web server (see attached file). It's recommended to make a backup of "render.js" before making changes. For existing projects, replace "render.js" in the project directory (e.g., C:\Users\[user_name]\Documents\NetBeansProjects\lwe1\js). For new projects, update "render.js" in the installation folder for the [product_name] Web Editor (e.g., C:\Program Files\lwe\lwe\res\web\edit\js).
Is it possible to simply open "render.js" with Notepad, make adjustments, and save it?
Yes, that works fine. As an alternative, I used the free "Notepad++" for editing.
Initially, it didn’t seem to work after updating the render file. But after clearing the browser history and logging in again, it worked as expected!
I assumed users would realize that when the web server page is new for the [product_name], refreshing the web browser is needed.
I refreshed the web page and logged in several times without success. It wasn’t until I deleted history in Google Chrome, refreshed, and logged in that the "16#" finally disappeared.
The solution works well for me, but on a different computer, I still see "16#" even after clearing browser history, cache, and cookies.
I can’t provide a definitive answer. When I access the extended web server from another device (PC, phone, tablet), I don’t encounter the issue.
I tried with a third computer and it worked, which suggests it may be related to browser cache. Thank you for testing.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced an issue in the extended web server for a [company_name] product where analog values appeared with a "16#" hex indicator. Editing the 'render.js' file typically resolved the problem, but some users found the issue persisted until browser history and cache were cleared. Effectiveness of the fix varied between devices, indicating inconsistencies in browser cache management when server-side files are updated.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that after updating the relevant web server file, the unwanted hex marker will consistently disappear across all devices and browsers when using the [product_name] web interface.
